summary.text: Defines the health worker cadres covered by the OptimizeMNH guideline, such as advanced-level and mid-level associate clinicians, auxiliary nurses, auxiliary midwives, nurses, midwives, lay health workers and doctors. For each it gives typical training, scope of practice and alternative job titles used in different countries. A note explains that the WHO definition of a midwife is used, although other sources define it slightly differently.

sections.title: Резюме

summary.text: The summary explains that health worker shortages threaten the health-related Millennium Development Goals and that redistributing tasks among cadres is a promising way to widen access and improve cost-effectiveness. It notes that results vary with local conditions, so it is important to define which key interventions different workers can deliver safely and effectively.

sections.extract: Дефицит кадровых ресурсов в области здравоохранения является общепризнанной угрозой для достижения связанных со здоровьем Целей развития тысячелетия (ЦРТ). Поэтому попытки оптимизировать потенциал имеющейся в наличии армии работников здравоохранения имеют решающее значение. Более рациональное распределение задач и обязанностей между кадрами медицинских работников рассматривается в качестве перспективной стратегии

sections.title: Цели

summary.text: States that the guideline aims to give evidence-based recommendations for widening access to key maternal and newborn interventions by optimising health worker roles, for policy-makers and managers to adapt to national contexts.

sections.extract: Эти рекомендации были разработаны в рамках мандата Всемирной организации здравоохранения для обеспечения нормативного руководства для государств- членов. Цель данного руководства заключается в выпуске научно обоснованных рекомендаций для расширения всеобщего доступа к основным эффективным мерам по улучшению здоровья матерей и новорожденных детей посредством оптимизации функций медицинских работников. sections.title: Методы разработки руководства

summary.text: Describes how the guideline followed the WHO handbook for guideline development, using GRADE evidence profiles from systematic reviews supplemented by qualitative and implementation evidence, presented through the DECIDE framework. It defines the four recommendation categories: recommended, recommended with targeted monitoring and evaluation, recommended only in the context of rigorous research, and not recommended.

sections.extract: Процедуры, используемые в разработке данного руководства, изложены в Справочнике ВОЗ по составлению руководств (1). sections.title: Рекомендации

summary.text: Reports that an international guideline panel meeting in Geneva in April and June 2012 made 119 recommendations, giving the number for each cadre from lay health workers to doctors. It notes the panel excluded self-administered misoprostol and did not cover community use of prefilled auto-disable injectable contraceptives, and points to Chapter 4 and the annexes for the full evidence.

summary.text: Explains that health system arrangements and social, cultural and political factors will shape implementation, so national dialogue is needed on whether shortages of skilled workers limit access and which cadres could take on tasks. It stresses that task shifting aims to reduce inequity while keeping care safe, mentions a practical adaptation guide in Annex 8, and advises treating recommendations as packages by topic and cadre.

summary.text: Lists the tasks the panel recommends for each type of health worker, starting with lay health workers promoting care-seeking, birth preparedness, insecticide-treated nets, HIV testing, exclusive breastfeeding, immunisation and kangaroo care. Further lists cover auxiliary nurses, auxiliary midwives, nurses, midwives and associate clinicians, some with targeted monitoring and evaluation. The list ends with external cephalic version for breech presentation by non-specialist doctors under targeted monitoring.

sections.title: Введение

summary.text: Introduces task shifting, or task sharing, as a way to widen access by training staff to take on functions they did not previously perform, potentially improving use of the workforce and care quality. It explains the choice of the term optimising delivery of key effective interventions and notes the guideline was developed under WHO Guidelines Review Committee standards with a focus on adaptation and implementation.

sections.title: Глобальный кризис трудовых ресурсов здравоохранения

summary.text: Describes the global health workforce crisis, noting that 57 countries had critical shortages in 2006, 36 of them in sub-Saharan Africa. That region has 11% of the world's population and 24% of the disease burden but only 3% of health workers and 1% of health spending, in contrast to the Americas, and many countries lack specialists such as surgeons and anaesthetists.

По данным Доклада о состоянии здравоохранения в мире за 2006 год, 57 стран испытывают хронический дефицит кадров в секторе здравоохранения. summary.text: Describes shortages in maternal and newborn health care, noting that about 52 million women give birth each year without a skilled attendant and coverage is below 50% in much of South Asia and sub-Saharan Africa. It notes slow progress in coverage and an inverse link between mortality and skilled attendance, calling for active workforce policies.

sections.title: Оптимизация функций работников здравоохранения посредством перераспределения обязанностей: общие принципы

summary.text: Sets out general principles for optimising health worker roles through task shifting, describing efforts since the Millennium Development Goals to raise skilled birth attendance and access to sexual and reproductive health services. It notes that some countries have trained lay health workers and other cadres to deliver specific interventions, especially in remote areas. It concludes that countries should adapt the recommendations to their political and health system contexts.

sections.extract: здравоохранения посредством перераспределения обязанностей: общие принципы Национальные стратегии в области здравоохранения способствуют повышению как уровня доступа, так и качества медицинской помощи. После одобрения ЦРТ во всем мире в странах с низким и средним уровнем дохода были предприняты дальнейшие усилия по улучшению здоровья матерей и новорожденных детей посредством повышения уровня квалифицированной помощи

sections.title: Выявление критически важных вопросов и результатов

summary.text: Describes how the key questions and outcomes were identified for WHO's guideline on optimising health worker roles for maternal and newborn health, in its Russian edition. Need was assessed through an online survey of priorities, which drew 393 responses mostly from low- and middle-income countries, and through requests from Member States, for example about misoprostol use by lay health workers. The section also describes the guideline development group, the technical secretariat, an online stakeholder consultation with participants from 33 countries, and a scoping meeting. It ends by explaining that changes that would turn a worker into a different cadre were not treated as task shifting.

sections.title: Получение доказательств

summary.text: Describes the three types of evidence used: effectiveness studies of interventions by specific cadres, qualitative studies of factors affecting task-shifting programmes, and country case studies of large-scale programmes. It explains that Cochrane systematic reviews were the main source of effectiveness evidence and were updated where needed. It also outlines how qualitative evidence and country case studies were searched for and synthesised, including a cross-cutting analysis structured by WHO health system building blocks.

sections.title: Формулирование рекомендаций

summary.text: Describes how recommendations were formulated at two technical consultations in April and June 2012, the second on contraception only, and why recommendations on antiretroviral therapy were removed to align with newer WHO HIV guidance. It explains how the group weighed benefits and harms, and covers declarations of interest. It also notes that no recommendation was made on lay workers giving injectable contraceptives with prefilled devices pending a study, and describes document preparation and external peer review.

summary.text: Introduces the evidence and recommendations section, explaining that recommendations, justifications and conditions are given for each cadre, with general implementation considerations in Box 1.

sections.extract: В последующих разделах по каждому вопросу представлены рекомендации, обоснования и условия в отношении каждой категории работников здравоохранения. sections.title: Мероприятия, рассматриваемые с точки зрения возможности их проведения непрофессиональными работниками здравоохранения

summary.text: Sets out recommendations on which maternal and newborn health tasks lay health workers should perform, presented as tables of questions, recommendations and justifications. Topics include health promotion, preventing and treating postpartum haemorrhage with oxytocin or misoprostol, distributing supplements, continuous support in labour and initial antibiotics for sepsis. It also covers kangaroo mother care, neonatal resuscitation and contraception, with some options recommended, some only under targeted research or monitoring and others not recommended. Implementation considerations include support systems for lay workers, confidentiality and training that stresses they should not set their own criteria for contraceptive eligibility.

sections.title: Мероприятия, рассматриваемые с точки зрения возможности их выполнения младшими медсестрами

summary.text: Sets out recommendations on tasks for auxiliary nurses, including oxytocin and misoprostol for postpartum haemorrhage and injectable antibiotics for premature rupture of membranes. It also covers kangaroo mother care, neonatal sepsis treatment, neonatal resuscitation, specific interventions in pregnancy and childbirth, and contraception. Implementation notes include considering female providers and trainers for reproductive health services and ensuring training in communication and side effects. It ends with a list of tasks considered already within this cadre's scope, for which evidence was not assessed.

summary.text: Sets out recommendations on tasks for auxiliary nurse midwives, noting that no recommendation was made on giving misoprostol to pregnant women for self-administration pending further research. Further tables cover postpartum haemorrhage, antibiotics, kangaroo care, neonatal resuscitation, interventions in pregnancy and childbirth, and contraception. It ends with training and confidentiality considerations and lists tasks considered within their existing scope.

sections.title: Мероприятия, рассматриваемые в отношении младших клиницистов повышенной квалификации

summary.text: Presents, in the Russian edition of WHO's OptimizeMNH recommendations on task shifting for maternal and newborn health, the interventions considered for advanced level associate clinicians, starting with external cephalic version for breech presentation, suggested only in the context of rigorous research. It sets out recommendations on clinical interventions such as vacuum extraction, which is recommended, and loading and maintenance doses of magnesium sulphate for eclampsia, suggested with targeted monitoring and evaluation. It closes with a list of further interventions covered, including magnesium sulphate for fetal neuroprotection and contraceptive methods such as injectables, IUDs, implants, tubal ligation and vasectomy.

summary.text: Sets out the intervention considered for non-specialist doctors, external cephalic version for breech presentation at term, suggested with targeted monitoring and evaluation based on low to moderate certainty evidence of benefit. It adds general implementation considerations for planners shifting tasks between cadres, such as regulation, training, supervision, referral, supply chains and incentives. It stresses that task shifting should come with a comprehensive pay scheme reflecting changes in workload.

sections.title: Финансирование

summary.text: Summarizes financing barriers to task shifting, including unclear roles and financial authority between national and local bodies and limited local financial management skills, and notes that fee-for-service payment can make doctors see task shifting as a threat to their income.

sections.extract: Распределение средств и управление ими. Выявленные проблемы включают отсутствие четкого понимания функций, финансовой ответственности и полномочий национальных и субнациональных структур, отсутствие знаний и надлежащих руководств по управлению финансами на местном уровне обслуживания. Методы оплаты. Выбор метода оплаты может влиять на мотивацию медицинского работника. Он также может влиять на отношения между самими

sections.title: Доступ к изделиям и средствам

summary.text: Notes that shortages of medicines and supplies and poor transport can hamper task shifting, affecting home visits, supervision and referrals, and states that the findings come from five implementation studies and a stakeholder survey.

sections.extract: Дефицит лекарств и изделий может отрицательно повлиять на реализацию программы и перераспределение обязанностей. Неразвитая транспортная инфраструктура также может повлиять на возможность медицинских работников посещать пациентов на дому, на возможность районных инспекторов обеспечивать контроль над работниками здравоохранения и на направление пациентов в медицинские учреждения. sections.title: Управление и руководство

summary.text: Explains how social values and political ideology shape decisions on implementing health programmes and equity goals, citing Brazil, where municipalities decide whether and how to run the Family Health Programme, which appears to have strengthened local ownership. It notes that local authorities may lack decision-making powers or face problems managing funds.

sections.extract: Сложившиеся в обществе представления и ценности могут повлиять на решения о реализации программ в области здравоохранения и принятие таких программ на местном уровне. Аналогичным образом, политическая идеология может повлиять на то, как распределяется ответственность за здравоохранение среди различных государственных структур, и на готовность местных органов управления реализовывать программы с учетом определенных

sections.title: Предоставление услуг

summary.text: Describes how task shifting can change health workers' roles and relationships, for example disrupting midwives' one-to-one care or raising the status of lay health workers. It reports that workers taking on tasks value recognition but may become dissatisfied without adequate training, support, clear responsibilities, malpractice cover and incentives, while more highly trained staff accept shifting routine tasks but worry about oversight and accountability. It also discusses interprofessional relations and patient relationships, noting that shifting care for stigmatized conditions to workers from the same community may raise confidentiality concerns.

sections.extract: Влияние перераспределения обязанностей на функции и должностные характеристики работников здравоохранения. Перераспределение обязанностей может привести к изменениям содержания определенных функций медицинских работников в более широком контексте организации, изменить деловые отношения и отношения между различными компонентами системы здравоохранения. Передача более сложных задач акушеркам, например, может нарушить

sections.title: Трудовые ресурсы здравоохранения

summary.text: Summarizes workforce issues in task shifting, including poor-quality or impractical training, unqualified trainers and unrealistic requirements, and stresses that training should match workers' new roles. It describes the need for emotional and professional support alongside clinical supervision, the barriers to good supervision and the value of on-site supervision and peer interaction.

sections.extract: Профессиональная подготовка перед поступлением на работу и в процессе работы. Проблемы включают неудовлетворительное качество подготовки, обучение, не отвечающее практическим потребностям, отсутствие надлежащей квалификации у инструкторов, негибкое расписание занятий, нереалистичные и недостижимые требования обучения. По результатам анализа можно сделать вывод о том, что подготовка должна проводиться с учетом

sections.title: Контекстуализация руководства

summary.text: Explains how countries can contextualize the OptimizeMNH guidance using the eight-step SUPPORT framework for evidence-informed health system policy, starting with identifying the right policy body and timing. It walks through the steps of clarifying the problem, framing options, identifying implementation considerations and examining the wider health and political systems. It ends with monitoring and evaluation needs and developing national recommendations, supported by structured policy briefs and policy dialogues.

sections.extract: процедуры разработки политики, чтобы определить надлежащий орган (например, национальная группа по составлению руководств или министерство здравоохранения), в который можно направить такое руководство. Этот этап важен для определения надлежащей формы продукта, аудитории, формата и языка, на котором будут составляться рекомендации или формулироваться политические решения. sections.title: Выводы по итогам исследований

summary.text: Sets out research gaps identified by the guideline group, suggesting future research should assess packages of interventions rather than single ones and compare different team compositions. It lists specific research questions by cadre, such as how non-maternal tasks affect midwives, what influences the performance of associate clinicians and how nurse availability compares with doctor availability in rural areas.

sections.extract: в пакеты (например, эффективность использования младших медицинских сестер для выполнения определенных задач, относящихся к деторождению), а не отдельных мероприятий (например, эффективность использования непрофессиональных работников здравоохранения для введения мизопростола в целях предотвращения послеродового кровотечения). Это составило бы более целостный подход к сложным вопросам функционирования систем

sections.title: Распространение рекомендаций

summary.text: Describes plans to disseminate the recommendations through WHO channels, the WHO website and the Reproductive Health Library with an independent AGREE appraisal, and a policy brief for country offices. It stresses well-planned national adaptation and implementation processes and notes that WHO and the Norwegian Knowledge Centre are user-testing the evidence-to-decision framework used in the guidance.

sections.extract: организации. Они также будут опубликованы на веб- сайте ВОЗ и размещены в Библиотеке репродуктивного здоровья ВОЗ (30), где будут сопровождаться независимой критической оценкой, проведенной в соответствии с Инструментом оценки качества клинических руководств (AGREE) (дополнительная информация приведена на сайте www.agreetrust.org). sections.title: Пересмотр и обновление рекомендаций

summary.text: Notes that the user testing, described on the DECIDE collaboration website, will inform future revisions, and states that the recommendations will be updated within five years, by 2018, unless new evidence requires earlier change.

sections.extract: хорошо работает эта система в качестве инструмента для представления доказательств и принятия решений в рамках работы групп по составлению руководств (более подробную информацию можно найти по адресу: www. decide-collaboration.eu). Эта оценка также понадобится при пересмотре руководства в будущем. Рекомендации будут обновлены через пять лет (к 2018 году), если не потребуется более раннее внесение изменений
